Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll start by reading the workspace contract, both required skill guides, and the inherited rollout artifacts. The visual-signals guide will determine how I inspect the 3D evidence before touching the policy; the fish-control shelf will constrain any mechanism transfer into the two-joint state-feedback contract.

The inherited lineage is already well past the naive seed: it has a coherent capture carrier and many completed terminal refinements. The durable evidence says the remaining mixed defect is route-integrated quality versus peak terminal yaw, while repeated fast residual gates and scalar reallocations have failed. I’m now comparing all four sampled rollouts—especially the best finite capture and the most informative weaker capture—before choosing whether a genuinely new mechanism is warranted.

The visual and numeric evidence agree: the two sampled sheets keep the same self-propelled, coherent alternating wake and smooth capture arc; the weaker role-separated policy is not a new topology. The sharper unused signal is in the controller’s main bearing-rate term: replaying the best trajectory shows its windowed bearing rate is still carrier-dominated (correlation `-0.931` with anterior joint rate), while the already calibrated anterior carrier subtraction reduces RMS from `1.599` to `0.429 rad/T` and nearly removes that correlation. I’m recording this observer hypothesis before editing, as required by the visual-evidence skill.

The candidate now makes one mechanism change only: it carries the existing anterior carrier estimate into the main bearing-trend observer, leaving every gain and both joint-actuation layers unchanged. I also revised the durable experience bank with the completed role-separation regression and the precise offline decorrelation boundary; it explicitly treats decorrelation as a hypothesis until CFD, not as a result. I’m moving through schema, syntax, and policy-contract checks now—without running CFD.

The mandated check-runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account, so it could not inspect the workspace. I’m executing its three declared checks directly and separately; this is the same non-CFD validation contract, and I’ll repair any substantive failure before finishing.

The guidance checker found a rendered-manifest defect rather than a policy defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent (`optimizer_17d60545469c`) twice, so the checker cannot select “exactly one” parent. I’m removing only that duplicate marker—without changing which parent is assigned—then rerunning the check.

Two of the three prescribed checks now pass: guidance semantics and solver boundary. The executable Julia smoke is blocked because this image has no `julia` binary (exit 127), so I’m replacing only that unavailable runtime signal with the deterministic schema/function audit required by the workspace, plus a focused source review of the changed expression.

Produced exactly one policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) applies bookshelf-informed carrier rejection to the main bearing-trend observer without retuning gains.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, evidence, transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:206) now captures the role-separation regression and carrier-correlation lesson.
- Removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md) so the mandatory checker could resolve the parent.

Guidance and boundary checks pass. Static audit found 73 parameter fields, 71 referenced fields, and no undeclared references. The prescribed check-runner was invoked but its pinned model is unsupported; the Julia smoke was also unavailable because Julia is not installed. No CFD was run.
